fixed_statement:
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem 1. Assume, toward contradiction, that \(M\) is not properly proximal.

There exists an \(M\)-central obstruction state \(\Omega\) on \(\mathcal N\), normal on \(M\), such that
\[
\Omega(q_K)=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\Omega(q_{U_i})=1
\qquad\text{for every }i=1,\dots,n.
\]
fixed_proof:
Since \(M\) has no amenable direct summand, the DKEP obstruction theorem gives an \(M\)-central obstruction state \(\Omega\) on \(\mathcal N\), normal on \(M\), such that
\[
\Omega(q_K)=0.
\]

For each \(i=1,\dots,n\), \(M\) is properly proximal relative to \(X_{U_i}\). Hence the second part of the obstruction theorem gives
\[
\Omega(q_{U_i})=1
\qquad\text{for every }i=1,\dots,n.
\]
